title: Schizophrenia: antipsychotic (dopamine D2 receptor antagonism)
vignette: A 22-year-old man is brought to the office by his mother due to a change in behavior over the past year. Nine months ago, the patient abruptly decided to quit college in his last year and insisted on moving back home to "work on my research without being disturbed." Since then, he has stopped going out with friends, seems uninterested in his usual hobbies of playing and watching football, and spends hours on his computer researching government cover-ups. He stays up late at night, sleeps during the day, and showers only once a week. The patient has no motivation to look for work; his mother reports that when she encourages him to go back to school or work, he becomes agitated and starts accusing her of "being one of the black suits." Physical examination shows poor hygiene but is otherwise normal. Laboratory evaluation, including urine drug screen, is unremarkable. A medication with which of the following primary mechanisms of action is most appropriate for this patient's condition?

clues.note: Continuous impairment for >=6 months (here ~9-12 months) meets the duration criterion for schizophrenia (vs shorter psychotic disorders).
Persistent, fixed false beliefs (paranoid/persecutory delusions) are a positive psychotic symptom of schizophrenia.
Avolition/apathy, social withdrawal, and self-neglect are NEGATIVE symptoms of schizophrenia.

clues.text: accusing her of "being one of the black suits."
clues.note: Paranoid/persecutory delusions (believing others are conspirators) support a psychotic disorder.

whatMatters: Delusions + negative symptoms (avolition, withdrawal, self-neglect) for >6 months with a normal drug screen = SCHIZOPHRENIA. First-line pharmacotherapy is an ANTIPSYCHOTIC, whose primary mechanism is DOPAMINE D2 RECEPTOR ANTAGONISM. Answer B.
strategy: Diagnose schizophrenia (>=2 core symptoms, >=6 months, functional decline, substances excluded), then recall antipsychotic mechanism: D2-receptor ANTAGONISM (second-generation agents add 5-HT2A antagonism). Reject serotonin reuptake inhibition (antidepressants - won't target psychosis), dopamine/norepinephrine reuptake inhibition (ADHD stimulants/bupropion - can worsen psychosis), GABA agonism (sedatives), alpha agonism, and antihistamines.

eliminations.label: Alpha receptor agonism - vasopressors/decongestants
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: alpha-adrenergic agonists (vasopressors, decongestants, clonidine). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: no therapeutic role in schizophrenia. ✅ Correct if: hypotension/decongestion or clonidine indications.

eliminations.label: Dopamine reuptake inhibition - stimulants (worsen psychosis)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increasing synaptic dopamine (stimulants). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: raising dopamine would WORSEN psychosis; antipsychotics BLOCK dopamine. ✅ Correct if: ADHD (methylphenidate) - not psychosis.

eliminations.label: GABA-A agonism - sedative-hypnotics
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: benzodiazepines/barbiturates/alcohol enhance GABA. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they sedate but don't treat the psychotic disorder. ✅ Correct if: acute agitation adjunct or sedation, not primary schizophrenia treatment.

eliminations.label: Histamine receptor antagonism - antihistamines
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: H1 blockers (sedation/allergy). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: not a treatment for schizophrenia (though antipsychotics have H1 side effects). ✅ Correct if: allergy/sedation.

eliminations.label: Norepinephrine reuptake inhibition - antidepressants/ADHD
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: NRI/SNRI mechanism. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: treats depression/ADHD, not psychosis. ✅ Correct if: depression or ADHD.

eliminations.label: Serotonin reuptake inhibition - SSRIs (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: SSRIs for depression/anxiety. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: SSRIs do not treat psychotic symptoms; schizophrenia needs a dopamine D2 antagonist (antipsychotic). ✅ Correct if: depression/anxiety, not psychosis.

reasoning: Delusions + negative symptoms + functional decline for >6 months, substances excluded = schizophrenia
First-line treatment is an antipsychotic medication
Antipsychotics act primarily by antagonizing postsynaptic dopamine D2 receptors
mechanism: Schizophrenia is diagnosed when a patient has >=2 core symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized/catatonic behavior, or negative symptoms - at least one being from the first three) for a significant portion of a month, with continuous signs for >=6 months and marked functional decline, and with mood disorders and substance/medical causes excluded (here the urine drug screen is normal). This patient shows positive symptoms (paranoid/persecutory delusions) and prominent NEGATIVE symptoms (avolition, social withdrawal, self-neglect). ANTIPSYCHOTIC medications are first-line, and their primary mechanism is ANTAGONISM at postsynaptic DOPAMINE D2 receptors (reducing dopaminergic overactivity in the mesolimbic pathway that underlies positive symptoms). Second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics add serotonin 5-HT2A antagonism (and some are D2 partial agonists), which improves negative symptoms and lowers extrapyramidal risk. The other listed mechanisms treat different disorders (antidepressants, stimulants, sedatives) or have no role in schizophrenia; increasing dopamine (reuptake inhibition) would actually worsen psychosis.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > schizophrenia: >=2 symptoms, >=6 months, functional decline; antipsychotics = D2 antagonists (atypicals also 5-HT2A antagonism); positive vs negative symptoms.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Chronic psychosis + negative symptoms = schizophrenia -> antipsychotic (D2 antagonism).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on positive vs negative symptoms, delusion, avolition, D2 antagonism, or atypical antipsychotics? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: SSRIs/SNRIs (depression), stimulants (worsen psychosis), GABA agonists (sedation), antihistamines don't treat psychosis.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: schizophrenia first-line = antipsychotic (D2 antagonism); atypicals add 5-HT2A antagonism.

keywords.back: Avolition, flat affect, social withdrawal, alogia, anhedonia

keywords.front: Why not raise dopamine in psychosis

firstAid.detail: Psych > SSRIs (depression), stimulants (ADHD), GABA (sedatives) - not psychosis.
Psych > >=2 symptoms, >=6 months, functional decline; exclude substances.

memoryHook: Too much dopamine talks in delusions - so schizophrenia's first-line drug turns the volume DOWN by blocking D2; SSRIs are the wrong channel.
